title: Aktarım Zinciri / The Transmission Chain
description:
An interactive bilingual (Turkish/English) study of how knowledge is transmitted between generations, built on a six-link transmission chain — packet, decoder, context, tacit knowledge, apparatus, maintenance — and tested against 32 real objects drawn from the modern-industrial, Ottoman and Roman worlds.

The repository contains three things:

  • The study (index.html): a single self-contained file with no external requests, no cookies and no analytics.
  • The corpus (data/): 255 dated, individually sourced transmission events across 32 objects, each coded to exactly one of six links under one fixed rule with no per-object tuning; plus 38 dated evidence records, a 32 × 6 model-coverage matrix, 275 unique sources, and a bilingual codebook.
  • The critique record (docs/): the adversarial review that produced the current version, and a version-by-version log of what was found wrong and corrected.

What this is not. It is a synthesis and a teaching instrument, not a research contribution. It has not been through human peer review; the scrutiny it has had is adversarial critique carried out by AI models from six specialist framings, and the writing, code, source checking and prior-art survey were done with AI assistance. Both facts are stated in the work itself and should travel with any reuse. The model parameters are assumed, not measured.

Known limits, stated by the author. The link coding is by a single unblinded coder with no inter-rater statistic; the object set carries two selection biases running in opposite directions; no base rate can be computed from the corpus. The codebook states these in full.
